title: Flywheel Model
subtitle: Build momentum that gets easier over time not harder
useWhen: Your growth feels like pushing a boulder uphill. Every new customer takes the same effort as the last. You're working harder each quarter to hit the same numbers. Growth isn't compounding it's grinding.
howToUse: Jim Collins introduced the Flywheel concept in Good to Great (2001) as a metaphor for business momentum. A flywheel takes enormous effort to start spinning but gains momentum with every rotation until it becomes self-sustaining. Amazon's flywheel is the most famous example: lower prices attract more customers, who attract more sellers, who drive lower costs, which enable lower prices. Every business has the potential for a flywheel the question is whether you've designed it deliberately. AI can help you identify and map yours.
steps: Map the 4–6 steps of your potential flywheel before prompting.
Each step must logically lead to the next if the causality isn't clear, the flywheel won't spin
Identify the one step in the flywheel that you need to push hardest right now.

Track flywheel velocity: how long does it take for a new customer to generate another? Not every business has a real flywheel, sometimes what looks like one is just a list of good things that happen to be true, with no actual causality between them. If step 3 doesn't clearly cause step 4, you've drawn a diagram, not a mechanism. Not Every Business Has One
origin: Jim Collins, Good to Great, 2001 — Flywheel concept · Amazon application, 2002
promptBody:
Act as a business strategy advisor using Jim Collins' Flywheel model.
My business                     :  [DESCRIBE WHAT YOU DO AND YOUR GROWTH MODEL]
Current growth drivers :  [WHAT IS WORKING TO GROW THE BUSINESS]
Biggest friction points   :  [WHERE GROWTH SLOWS OR STOPS]
Step 1  :  Map my business flywheel.
Identify 4–6 steps that form a self-reinforcing loop. Each step must logically cause the
next.
Step 2 :  Name the flywheel - what is the core mechanism that drives it?
Step 3 :  Identify which step in the flywheel has the most friction right now.
Step 4 :  Suggest 2 specific actions to reduce friction at that step and accelerate the spin.
Compare my flywheel to Amazon's - what is similar and what is fundamentally different?
Flywheel Model — Momentum That Compounds
Self-Sustaining
Lower Prices
Lower Costs
More Sellers
More Customers
Lower Prices
proTip:
Most founders try to build a flywheel at the business level before they have one at the
customer level. Your first flywheel is simpler: a happy customer refers someone, that
person becomes a customer, their success becomes your proof, proof attracts the next
customer. Map that loop first and invest in making it spin faster.
